blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Most companies end up with far more software than anybody realised. A new tool is signed up by marketing. Another is trialled by sales. A third is adopted quietly by finance. After a few years, the company is paying for dozens of tools, many overlapping and some forgotten entirely.

Managing the portfolio actively means doing two boring things well. First, a real list of every tool the company is paying for should be kept, with its owner, its renewal date and its actual user count. Second, that list should be reviewed every six months, removing anything that is no longer used and questioning anything that overlaps with another tool.

A clean portfolio costs less, creates fewer security risks and — quietly — makes the company easier to support. None of this is exciting. All of it pays off every quarter it is done.

items.q: According to the text, why do companies end up with so much software?
options: Different teams sign up, trial and adopt tools separately over time
IT insists on buying new tools every year
Vendors force long contracts on the company
The finance team refuses to cancel anything
items.why: "signed up by marketing… trialled by sales… adopted quietly by finance" — cada área adota por conta própria.

items.q: What are the two "boring things" the text recommends?
options: Keeping a real list of tools and reviewing it every six months
items.why: "keep a real list… review that list every six months."

items.q: The text says a clean portfolio does all of the following EXCEPT…
options: makes the company easier to support
items.why: O texto cita custo, segurança e suporte — nunca receita de vendas.

items.q: The phrase "None of this is exciting. All of it pays off" suggests that the author…
options: values steady, unglamorous discipline over novelty
thinks companies should hire consultants instead
believes the work is too dull to be worth doing
prefers buying new tools to reviewing old ones
items.why: Inferência: o autor defende exatamente o trabalho chato e constante porque ele compensa.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Software should have a named owner and a renewal date.
Reviewing the portfolio regularly reduces risk.
A tool that no one uses should still be kept just in case.
items.why: Inferência: o texto manda remover o que não é mais usado — manter "por via das dúvidas" contraria a tese.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry conduzindo a revisão de software. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time. I've spent the last two weeks going through everything we pay for, and I want to walk you through what I found before anyone panics.

We are currently paying for sixty-one tools. Of those, eighteen have not been opened by a single person in the last ninety days. Not one login. And on top of that, I found four pairs of tools that do essentially the same job — two of them are both project trackers, and honestly nobody could tell me why we have both.

Now, I'm not here to point fingers. Every one of these was adopted for a good reason at the time. But a licence that could be cancelled tomorrow is money that could be spent somewhere it actually helps. So here's what I'd suggest. For the eighteen with no users, we send one message to each owner: if nobody objects within two weeks, the tool is switched off. For the overlapping pairs, let's sit down and pick one each.

None of this needs to be dramatic. It just needs to be done, and then done again in six months. If we don't build the habit, we'll be right back here next year with an even longer list.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many tools is the company currently paying for?
items.why: "We are currently paying for sixty-one tools."

items.q: What is true of the eighteen tools Harry highlights?
options: No one has logged into them in the last ninety days
items.why: "eighteen have not been opened by a single person in the last ninety days. Not one login."

items.q: What does Harry propose for the eighteen unused tools?
options: Cancel them all immediately without warning
Message each owner and switch the tool off if no one objects in two weeks
Keep them until the next annual audit
Move them to a different department
items.why: "we send one message to each owner: if nobody objects within two weeks, the tool is switched off."

items.q: When Harry says "I'm not here to point fingers," he most likely wants to…
options: avoid blaming colleagues so they cooperate with the cleanup
items.why: Inferência: ele desarma a defensiva para que a conversa sobre remover ferramentas ande.

items.q: What does Harry imply will happen if they don't build the review habit?
options: The problem will return, larger, next year
Security will improve on its own
items.why: Inferência: "we'll be right back here next year with an even longer list" — sem o hábito, o problema volta maior.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Two of our tools clearly overlap — they do almost the same job." An overlap is…
options: a gap where no tool exists
an area where two things cover the same function
a discount for buying in bulk
items.why: Overlap = sobreposição: duas ferramentas cobrindo a mesma função.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before we commit, let's ___ the platform with one team for a month."
items.why: To trial = testar antes de adotar de vez.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We almost auto-renewed a licence nobody uses because we missed the ___."
items.why: Renewal date = data de renovação, quando a licença se renova automaticamente.

items.q: "The tool only has three active users, so its user count doesn't justify the cost." User count means…
options: the number of people actually using it
the number of features it offers
items.why: User count = número de usuários que de fato usam a ferramenta.

items.q: "None of this is exciting, but cleaning up the portfolio will pay off." To pay off means to…
options: produce a worthwhile result over time
settle a debt with the vendor
items.why: To pay off = compensar, trazer retorno com o tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem numa revisão de portfólio de software. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "IT still has to sign off on switching the tool off." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new CRM to one region before the rest." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A few teams pushed back on removing their favourite app." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to audit the portfolio but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Unapproved apps that staff install on their own are called shadow IT." This term refers to…
options: software the IT team builds in-house
items.why: Shadow IT = software não aprovado que as áreas adotam por conta própria, criando risco de segurança.
